prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To estimate a dollar range, I'd need: the actual medical bills/specials to date (ER, ambulance, right knee replacement surgery, ongoing treatment), the estimated cost of the still-pending left knee replacement surgery, any lost wage or lost earning capacity figures, any settlement demand or jury verdict amount if one has already been reached, and the specific dollar amount of Mississippi's statutory noneconomic damages cap as applied to this claim (and whether a catastrophic-injury exception to that cap is being asserted).
prediction.likelyOutcome: Womack is well positioned to prevail on liability given the general manager's documented proximity and sightline during the ten-minute window the hazard existed, and her causation theory for the knee injuries survived summary judgment and is now bolstered by a clarifying expert affidavit invoking reasonable medical probability. The principal remaining risks are a jury discounting notice given the short time window, apportioning causation substantially to preexisting end-stage osteoarthritis (especially for the un-imaged left knee), and the statutory noneconomic damages cap limiting recovery regardless of injury severity -- but none of the case materials provide the medical bills, surgery costs, lost wages, or stated cap figure needed to translate this favorable liability picture into a dollar range.

issues.label: Existence of an unreasonably dangerous condition (collapsed wet-floor sign)
Actual/constructive notice via general manager's proximity and sightline
Causation: fall caused meniscal tears and necessitated bilateral knee replacement

outcome.description: The jury found the defendants' negligence the sole proximate cause of the fall and awarded $393,000 in economic damages (past and future medical expenses) and $3,000,000 in noneconomic damages. The circuit court reduced the noneconomic award to the $1,000,000 statutory cap (Miss. Code Ann. 11-1-60(2)(b)), entering an amended final judgment for $1,393,000, and denied JNOV or new trial. The Court of Appeals of Mississippi, en banc, affirmed on December 17, 2024, rejecting the dangerous-condition, notice, expert and further-remittitur arguments. No attorney's fees.
